env_overrides.description:
Keys an `SQAIL_*` environment variable replaces; changing them in the
file has no effect.

settings.description: The settings as saved in the config file (without environment overrides).

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the served certificate, as clients pin it.

last_restart_error.description: Why the last restart from the admin page failed, if it did.

listen.description: The address the service listens on.

started_at.description: When the service process started (restarts from the admin page keep it).

urls.description:
Addresses clients can use (for a wildcard address: this host's name
and loopback).

log_sql.description: Record query text in the audit log (never row values).

max_sql_len.description: Truncate logged SQL to this many bytes.

actor.description: Token name, or `cli` for local administrative commands.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next (older) page.

path.description: The backup file, on the service host. `master.key` is not included.

key_pem.description: PEM private key (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1).

type_name.description: The engine's own type name, e.g. `int4`, `nvarchar`, `INTEGER`.

admin_ui.description:
Serve the admin page at `/admin/` and the `/v1/admin` API that
changes these settings.

bind.description: Address to listen on. Defaults to loopback only.

docs_ui.description: Serve the interactive API docs at `/docs`.

Connection.description: A stored connection profile as returned by the API (never includes secrets).

color.description: UI accent colour, e.g. `#c0392b` for production.

password.description: Write-only. On update: `None` keeps the stored password, `""` clears it.

ConnectionParams.description:
Engine-specific connection parameters. Secrets are *not* part of this type;
see [`ConnectionInput::password`].

CreatedToken.description: Returned once on creation; the secret is never retrievable again.

Engine.description: Database engines sqail knows how to talk to.

analyze.description:
Execute the statement to get actual row counts and timings. It runs
inside a transaction that is always rolled back (Postgres, SQL
Server); SQLite has no analyze mode and returns the estimated plan.

burst.description: Per-token burst on top of the sustained rate.

default_max_rows.description: Default row cap per result set when the request does not set one.

default_timeout_ms.description: Default query timeout when the request does not set one.

max_rows.description: Hard row cap per result set.

LogicalType.description:
How a column's cells are encoded in JSON and should be displayed.

Cell encoding: `null` for SQL NULL; otherwise `Bool` → bool, `Int` → number
(i64 — beware JavaScript clients past 2^53), `Float` → number (NaN/±Inf as
strings), `Bytes` → lowercase hex string, everything else → string
(`Decimal` keeps full precision, temporals are ISO-8601, `Json` is JSON text).

oneOf.description: SQL Server login; the password goes in [`ConnectionInput::password`].
Windows integrated auth (only when the service runs on Windows).

Param.description: A bind parameter. JSON `null`, booleans, numbers and strings map directly.

raw.description: The engine's own output (JSON, XML or text).

PlanNode.description: One operator in a query plan, engine-neutral.

actual_ms.description: Actual time of this subtree in ms (analyze only, Postgres).

cost.description: Estimated cost of this subtree (engine units).

label.description: Operator, e.g. `Hash Join`, `Clustered Index Seek`, `SCAN orders`.

object.description: Object the operator works on (table/index), when known.

Problem.description: Error body for every non-2xx response (`application/problem+json`).

QueryEvent.description:
One line of a streamed query response.

Order: `started`, then for every statement either
`result_start` → `rows`* → `result_end`, or `rows_affected`; `message`s may
appear anywhere; finally exactly one `done`. An `error` ends the script
early but is still followed by `done`.

truncated.description: `max_rows` was hit; further rows were discarded.

db_code.description: SQLSTATE (Postgres) or error number (SQL Server), when known.

in_transaction.description: Session queries only: whether a transaction is still open.

max_rows.description: Row cap *per result set*; the service enforces its own maximum.

sql.description:
One or more statements. SQL Server scripts may use `GO` separators.
With `params`, exactly one statement is allowed; placeholders are the
engine's native ones (`$1` Postgres, `@P1` SQL Server, `?1` SQLite).

port.description: The port the service will listen on after the restart.

Scope.description: What an API token may do. Ordered: `Admin` > `Query` > `Read`.

scope.description: Scope of the token that made the request.

idle_timeout_secs.description: Idle sessions are closed (and rolled back) after this many seconds.

allowed_dirs.description:
SQLite profiles may only point at files inside these directories.
Empty means SQLite is disabled.

create.description: Create the file if it does not exist.

path.description:
Absolute path on the *service* host. Must be inside one of the
service's allowed SQLite directories.

cert.description:
PEM certificate chain. When absent a self-signed dev certificate is
generated in `<data_dir>/tls/`.

client_ca.description:
Mutual TLS: require client certificates signed by this CA (PEM).
Bearer tokens are still required on top.

info.description: HTTPS gateway between sqail2 and SQL databases. Query results stream as NDJSON (`application/x-ndjson`), one `QueryEvent` per line.
info.title: sqail-service

post.summary: Write a consistent copy of `service.db` to `<data-dir>/backups/`.

Store a certificate and key in `<data-dir>/tls/`. They take effect once
the settings point `tls.cert` and `tls.key` at the returned paths.
Re-read the config file and restart.

get.summary: The settings in the config file.

put.summary:
Check new settings, then restart the service with them. They are saved
to the config file once the service runs with them; if it cannot start,
it goes back to the previous settings and `/v1/admin/status` reports why.
Open sessions are closed and running queries cancelled.

Run a script on the session's connection. One query at a time per session.
Create a token. The secret is returned once and never stored in clear.
